task.title: Draft the v2.1 release notes for enterprise customers
task.goal: Formal tone, foregrounding compliance and performance as the two throughlines, ready to publish as-is

userStory.trigger: v2.1 ships next week and needs public-facing release notes
userStory.goal: Get a formal release-notes draft that foregrounds customer value
userStory.reads: The agent's read on your intent, the structure and tradeoffs it has chosen, and the style and compliance wording still undecided
userStory.acts: Adopt the structure as final / change the brief and rewrite / make the call on the pending sections and wording

observablePrimitives.label: User brief: formal, foreground compliance and performance

nodes.title: Audience = enterprise IT decision-makers; tone formal; must cover compliance and performance

steps.observed: fixed the audience and the two throughlines per the user brief

nodes.title: Reordering how it's organized
nodes.from: List the changes one by one, feature by feature
nodes.to: Organize by customer value: three columns — compliance / performance / availability
nodes.rationale: Enterprise decision-makers care about "what this means for me"; a value-led framing fits the audience and the formal tone better than a feature list.

nodes.title: Adopt the three-column value structure, with one quantified benefit per item

evidence.label: all 37 changes fit into the three columns

steps.observed: quantified benefits come from the benchmark comparison
changes sort cleanly into three columns

nodes.title: A flat list by feature module
nodes.reason: Too dense for enterprise decision-makers and the value doesn't stand out — at odds with the purpose of formal release notes.

nodes.title: Whether to add a "Upgrading from v1" section
nodes.falsification: If most target customers are still on v1, an upgrade guide is clearly useful; need product to confirm the v1 install base before deciding.

nodes.title: Two pieces of compliance wording need legal / marketing sign-off
nodes.needs: The two public-facing lines — "certified to XX" and "compliant with YY regulation" — require legal sign-off and a unified marketing line.

outcome.label: Draft delivered · Grounded
outcome.text: Produced a three-column value-structured draft (compliance/performance/availability), each item with a quantified benefit.
outcome.recommendation: Finalize once the v1 install base is confirmed (deciding the upgrade guide) and the legal wording is settled.

steps.label: Understand the ask
steps.hint: First anchor the user's intent and constraints as a requirement (audience / tone / the two throughlines).

steps.label: Inflection
steps.hint: Aha: shift from a feature list to a three-column value framing, and the flat list settles.

steps.label: Structure decided
steps.hint: The three-column structure crystallizes into a grounded decision, each item with a quantified benefit.

steps.label: Pending confirmation
steps.hint: Honestly leaves it: the upgrade guide awaits data, the compliance wording awaits legal.
